name: Pickup
description: A bubble of pulp bursting against the mouth: one sine dropping from $tonic to $third.down in 45ms, a pop rather than a beep. It fires in streams — a magnet pulls a whole field in at once — so it is built to pile up like a pan of something simmering, never like a machine: a pure tone with nothing above it, four takes of different size and shape the engine turns through (the plain pop, a bigger slower bwop, a small quick pip that barely falls, and a pop that splits in two), a pitch rolled wide on top of each, and no more than a dozen of it a second. The takes are written by hand rather than with `takes`, because a pure tone has nothing to reseed; they carry the `take-N` names so the engine round-robins them all the same.

take-2.description: Bwop: the same pop from a bigger bubble — a fifth-ish lower and a quarter longer.

take-3.description: Pip: a small quick one that only falls to $third, so it reads as a lighter, brighter pop.

take-4.description: Pop-pop: the bubble splits, and a smaller second pop follows the first 30ms later.
